title: Brown rice with tomatoes and/or tomato-based sauce, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice is the whole‑grain version of rice that retains the bran and germ. In this product the rice is cooked together with tomatoes or a tomato‑based sauce and a fat (oil or butter) is added to enhance flavor and aid the absorption of fat‑soluble nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice contains more fiber and nutrients than white rice because it is not milled.
Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
Adding fat helps the body absorb lipophilic compounds from tomatoes such as lycopene and carotenoids.
Many traditional cuisines (e.g., Spanish paella) combine rice, tomatoes and oil as a classic flavor base.
Brown rice has a lower glycemic index than white rice, making it better for blood‑sugar control.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health, promotes satiety and helps maintain regular bowel movements.

items.title: Source of magnesium and selenium
items.content: These minerals are important for muscle function, the nervous system and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Contains lycopene and other antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes provide lycopene, which may reduce the risk of certain chronic diseases, including heart disease.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: The combination of healthy fats and antioxidants can help lower LDL cholesterol levels.

items.title: Steady energy release
items.content: Complex carbohydrates in brown rice provide a gradual release of glucose, sustaining energy over time.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Brown rice contains phytic acid, which can bind minerals and reduce their absorption when consumed in excess.

items.title: Fat intolerance or allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive or allergic to added animal or plant fats.

items.title: Arsenic levels
items.content: Like most rice, brown rice may contain trace amounts of arsenic; it is advisable to vary grain sources.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The added fat increases the calorie count, so portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rice as a side dish with meat, fish or vegetables, incorporate it into casseroles, salads or soups. Before serving, stir in fresh tomatoes or tomato sauce and a drizzle of oil (olive, sunflower or butter) for aroma and richness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked rice with tomatoes and fat should be cooled quickly and stored in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. It can be frozen for up to 2 months.
